answer.rationale: Two of the three current signals are funnel-health problems (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%), and only one lever addresses the upstream cause of both: onboarding friction. Promotional pricing is the tempting reflex given the competitor's entry pricing, but discounting price-sensitive SMBs buys acquisition at the cost of margin and retention quality, which conflicts with the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Referral incentives and enterprise sales-assist are healthy plays but target segments that are not where the decay is showing. Activation messaging treats the symptom downstream of a funnel that is leaking earlier. I am therefore inclined to confirm the provisional direction, but the provisional direction is exactly what deserves the scrutiny rather than a free pass, so I am spending the single verification pull on memory_86 — the most load-bearing evidence for it (day 52, shortening onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value across self-serve accounts). I want to check whether that lift was measured on completion rate alone or carried through to activation and retained revenue, and whether the tested population resembles today's affected accounts. If the original record shows the gain was a shallow completion-metric artifact that never converted into durable revenue, then the provisional direction is resting on a weaker foundation than it appears and I would shift toward activation_messaging, which memory_91 ties more directly to first meaningful action. Verifying memory_31 instead would be redundant, since it points the same way and covers signup rather than onboarding.
